questions.prompt: When facing a Merge sign a driver should:
questions.explanation: A merge sign means two lanes of traffic are joining. Use the acceleration lane to match highway speed, find a gap, and blend in smoothly. Don't stop unless you have to.

choices.text: Stop at the entrance to the other highway and wait until a gap in traffic occurs before proceeding
Watch for a gap in traffic on the highway they are entering, adjust to highway speed in the acceleration lane and blend in smoothly
Stop and yield the right-of-way to traffic already on the highway
Reduce speed and proceed with caution

questions.prompt: A deceleration lane is:
questions.explanation: A deceleration lane is an exit lane where you slow down after leaving the highway, instead of slowing down in the traffic lanes. Key words: "deceleration lane".

choices.text: A lane where vehicles reduce speed when exiting a highway
The right lane of a four-lane highway for use by slower moving vehicles
A lane on hills for use by slower moving vehicles
The lane immediately to the right of a solid yellow line on a highway

questions.prompt: An acceleration lane is:
questions.explanation: An acceleration lane is part of an on-ramp. It lets you speed up to match highway traffic before you merge. Key words: "acceleration lane".

choices.text: The left lane of a four-lane highway, for use when passing slow moving vehicles
A lane on hills, designated for faster moving vehicles
A lane in a merge area for use by vehicles entering the highway
A lane with broken line markings

questions.prompt: Is a driver allowed to exceed the speed limit when passing another vehicle?
questions.explanation: The speed limit always applies, including while passing. If you can't pass without speeding, don't pass.

choices.text: Yes, on primary highways only
No, it is never permitted
Yes, but not more than 10 km/h over the speed limit
Only when passing more than one vehicle at a time

questions.prompt: A "weave zone" is best described as:
questions.explanation: In a weave zone, an entrance lane and an exit lane share the same stretch of road, so drivers entering and drivers exiting must cross paths. Watch carefully and adjust your speed. Key words: "entrance and exit lanes are close together".

choices.text: A place on a highway where the entrance and exit lanes are close together and vehicles that are slowing to exit the highway must drive between vehicles that are accelerating to enter the highway
A place where the highway has a series of curves that require the driver to slow down
An area on the highway that is used for emergency parking
A limited access area on a highway where a driver can legally back their vehicle when they miss their exit

questions.prompt: If a driver is being followed by a vehicle that is attempting to pass on a two-way road, the driver should:
questions.explanation: When someone is passing you, stay in your lane, move to the right portion of it, and don't speed up. This gives the passing driver more room. Key words: "right portion".

choices.text: Stay in the lane and move to the right portion of the lane
Turn on the right signal and drive in the parking lane
Turn on the left signal and stay in the lane
Stay in the lane and move to the left portion of the lane

questions.prompt: On a two-lane highway, when passing other vehicles travelling in the same direction, a driver:
questions.explanation: On a two-lane highway, pass on the left, and only when it is safe and legal to do so.

choices.text: Should pass on the left when safe
Should pass on the right when safe
Should always travel 30 km/h faster than the vehicle being passed
Should not pull out to pass until they are within 3 metres of the vehicle being passed

questions.prompt: When driving in the right lane on a highway, what should a driver do if another vehicle attempts to merge from an acceleration lane on the right?
questions.explanation: Help merging traffic in: move to the left lane if it is safe, or adjust your speed to leave a gap.

choices.text: Move into the left lane, if it is safe to do so, or be prepared to adjust speed
Stop to allow the other vehicle in
Accelerate to close any gap in the traffic flow
Insist that the other vehicle yield the right-of-way

questions.prompt: A "parking lane" as defined in the Basic License Driver's Handbook is:
questions.explanation: A "parking lane" is defined as that portion of a primary highway between the edge of the roadway (to the right for traffic) and the nearest solid white line (not the centerline), essentially the shoulder or curb area where parking is permitted unless signed otherwise

choices.text: A lane closest to the curb, where parking is permitted but there are no meters
That portion of a primary highway between the edge of the roadway to the right of the direction of traffic and the nearest solid white line, not being the centre line, marked on the roadway
A lane immediately beside a row of parking meters in an urban area
All of these responses are correct

questions.prompt: Where in your lane should you normally drive on a marked roadway?
questions.explanation: When a roadway is divided into lanes by visible markings, drive in the centre of your lane. (Driver's Guide p. 70)

choices.text: Close to the right edge of your lane
Close to the centre line
In the centre of your lane
Over the lane line, so others can see you

questions.prompt: Before changing lanes, in what order should you do these steps?
questions.explanation: Make sure a lane change is allowed, check your mirrors, shoulder check, signal, then move over while keeping your speed. (Driver's Guide p. 71)

choices.text: Signal, change lanes, then check your mirrors
Check mirrors, shoulder check, signal, then change lanes
Change lanes, then signal
Shoulder check, change lanes, then check mirrors

questions.prompt: On a multi-lane highway, which lane should slower traffic use?
questions.explanation: Slower traffic should use the travel lane furthest to the right, unless it needs the left lane to turn left. This leaves the left lane for passing. (Driver's Guide p. 71)

choices.text: The lane furthest to the left
The centre lane
Any lane
The lane furthest to the right

questions.prompt: On a highway with a passing lane, what should slower vehicles do?
questions.explanation: Slower vehicles move into the right lane so other vehicles can pass safely in the left lane. (Driver's Guide p. 71)

choices.text: Move into the right lane so others can pass on the left
Stay in the left lane and speed up
Pull onto the shoulder
Turn on their hazard lights and continue

questions.prompt: A passing lane is ending. Who must cooperate?
questions.explanation: Drivers in the right lane must merge safely to the left, and drivers in the left lane must cooperate to let them in. (Driver's Guide p. 71)

choices.text: Right-lane drivers merge left, and left-lane drivers help them in
Only right-lane drivers; left-lane drivers have the right-of-way
Only left-lane drivers, who must move right
Neither; vehicles should stop and take turns

questions.prompt: Before passing another vehicle on a two-lane highway, which way should you shoulder check?
questions.explanation: Shoulder check to the left, to look for vehicles that may be passing you on the left in your blind spot. (Driver's Guide p. 72)

choices.text: To the right
To the left
Over both shoulders
No shoulder check is needed when passing

questions.prompt: After passing a vehicle on a two-lane highway, when can you return to your lane?
questions.explanation: Once you can see the vehicle you passed in your inside rear-view mirror, shoulder check right, signal right, and return to your lane. (Driver's Guide p. 72)

choices.text: As soon as your front bumper passes the other vehicle
When you can see the passed vehicle in your inside rear-view mirror
When the other driver flashes their headlights
After counting to two

questions.prompt: In which situation is passing another vehicle not allowed?
questions.explanation: Do not pass when another vehicle has stopped to let a pedestrian cross at a marked or unmarked crosswalk. (Driver's Guide p. 72)

choices.text: When the centre line is broken and the road ahead is clear
When a vehicle has stopped for a pedestrian at a crosswalk
When you are on a multi-lane highway
When the vehicle ahead is going below the speed limit

questions.prompt: What is the emergency stopping lane of a highway for?
questions.explanation: The shoulder of a primary highway is for drivers who need to stop because of an urgent situation or a problem with their vehicle. (Driver's Guide pp. 72–73)

choices.text: Passing slower vehicles
Slower vehicles to drive in
Stopping in an emergency or when your vehicle has a problem
Waiting to merge onto the highway

questions.prompt: May you use the shoulder of a highway to pass a vehicle that is turning left?
questions.explanation: No. Do not drive in the emergency stopping lane, and do not pass, or help another vehicle pass you, by using it. (Driver's Guide p. 73)

choices.text: Yes, if the shoulder is paved
No, never use the shoulder for passing
Yes, if you signal first
Yes, at speeds under 50 km/h

questions.prompt: When merging onto a highway, who has the right-of-way?
questions.explanation: Neither the merging vehicle nor the vehicles already on the highway have the right-of-way. Merging is a shared responsibility. (Driver's Guide p. 73)

choices.text: Neither; merging is a shared responsibility
The merging vehicle
Vehicles already on the highway
Whichever vehicle is larger

questions.prompt: Why should you avoid stopping in an acceleration lane when merging?
questions.explanation: Merging lanes are designed for reaching highway speed. Drivers behind you expect you to keep moving, and you could be hit from behind if you slow or stop. (Driver's Guide p. 73)

choices.text: It is illegal to stop anywhere on a highway
It wastes fuel
Drivers behind you expect you to keep moving and could hit you
Merging traffic always has the right-of-way

questions.prompt: When merging from an acceleration lane, when may you move into the highway lane?
questions.explanation: When it is safe and legal, move into your chosen gap after you are past the solid white line of the acceleration lane. (Driver's Guide p. 73)

choices.text: As soon as you enter the acceleration lane
Only after coming to a complete stop
Only when there is no traffic at all
After you are past the solid white line, when it is safe

questions.prompt: You have missed your exit on a highway. What should you do?
questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, don't stop. Continue to the next exit and plan to return to your route. Never stop and reverse on a highway or its shoulder. (Driver's Guide p. 74)

choices.text: Stop on the shoulder and reverse to the exit
Continue to the next exit
Make a U-turn across the median
Slow down and cut across to the exit

questions.prompt: Where should you do most of your slowing when exiting a highway?
questions.explanation: If possible, do most of your slowing in the deceleration lane. Some are short, so you may need to start slowing on the highway. (Driver's Guide p. 74)

choices.text: In the highway lane before the exit
On the ramp after the deceleration lane
In the deceleration lane
On the shoulder

questions.prompt: When should you reduce your speed for a curve?
questions.explanation: If you need to reduce speed, do it before entering the curve, and keep a safe, steady speed through it. (Driver's Guide p. 75)

choices.text: In the middle of the curve
Before entering the curve
As you exit the curve
You shouldn't change speed for curves

questions.prompt: Your vehicle starts to skid on a curve. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Stay off the brake and the accelerator, look where you want to go, and make small steering adjustments. (Driver's Guide p. 75)

choices.text: Stay off the brake and gas, look and steer where you want to go
Brake hard and steer sharply
Accelerate to regain traction
Turn the wheel quickly in the opposite direction

questions.prompt: As you approach the top of a hill on a two-lane road, you should:
questions.explanation: Move to the right in your lane. This may keep you from being hit by an oncoming vehicle that has crossed the centre line. Don't pass near the top of a hill. (Driver's Guide p. 76)

choices.text: Move toward the centre line for a better view
Pass any slower vehicles before the crest
Move to the right side of your lane
Speed up to get over the hill quickly

questions.prompt: Going down a steep hill in a vehicle with a manual transmission, why shift to a lower gear?
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear can reduce the risk of your brakes overheating. (Driver's Guide p. 76)

choices.text: To reduce the risk of the brakes overheating
To save fuel
To go faster down the hill
It is required by law on all hills
